doc.title: Yusef Lateef — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Today's music, Coltrane and leading a band
title: Coltrane after A Love Supreme
summary: Lateef sees the later work as exploratory music that acts as a catalyst for others.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: What, what’s your opinion of, of uh John Coltrane’s, let’s say, post-A Love Supreme work? ‘Cause that, that seems to be uh–in fact, Katya[sp] and I were talking

about this fairly recently, that they’ve just reissued Ascension and, and Kulu Sé Mama and–I think your, your analogy is apt there. It’s like someone walking a person home and they say, “I’ll walk three blocks with you.” If the person lives six blocks away, they stop on the third block and go.
What, what is, what is your opinion of, of those, those latter works?

A Love Supreme. Well, I think they’re in that realm of uh exploratory music. Um...you know, I think music like that shows us that, it makes us think, “What is it can I do? What can I contribute to culture? This man has moved from A to Z, you know. So, what am I?” It’s motivating, I think. He shows you all these possibilities...and I think that’s what it serves as a catalyst for others to, to contribute.
